video_title: Jerome Bettis: “Lord, If This Is How You Want My Career to End.”

quotes.speaker: Jerome Bettis
quotes.summary_phrase: Jerome Bettis recalls his hardest hit against Brian Urlacher
quotes.excerpt: It was by far the hardest hit that I ever got because I didn't even see him.

text_blocks.speaker: Jerome Bettis
text_blocks.text: I go, I turn, I catch the ball. When I turn back, I see my offensive guard on the ground. I'm going. Well, I don't realize he had thrown him on the ground, so he's sitting there waiting on me. I jump over my guard. Head to the ground, boom first. I jump up. You never want to let them see you. But I'm in a million pieces. I'm broke. I'm broken. So I'm trying to keep it all in here because I'm struggling. So I'm head right to the sideline. I go right to the sideline. And they're like, no, no, no. I'm like, oh, I'm coming back. I'm sorry. I'm coming. I don't know what y'all are talking about. And I get a little closer. I'm running to the wrong sideline. I'm running to the wrong sideline. And they're like, I'm like, come back. And I'm like, I get all the way to the sideline and I just got to fall out. Boom. And it was by far the hardest hit that I ever got because I didn't even see him.

quotes.speaker: Jerome Bettis
quotes.summary_phrase: Jerome Bettis reflects on the iconic hit against Brian Urlacher
quotes.excerpt: He's my man, love him to death, but Urlacher, because he's my man.

text_blocks.speaker: Jerome Bettis
text_blocks.text: It's unfortunate because I love him to death. It's a shame we're having that boy over there. But Urlacher, because he's my man, love him to death. But the Super Bowl year, this was the moment that our season had to flip. We were in a situation where we were five and seven. If we lost another game, we were going to be out of the playoffs. So we ultimately ended up being the last team in the playoffs. And so that's the first time a last-place team in the playoffs won the Super Bowl.

text_blocks.speaker: Stephen Jackson
text_blocks.text: It's a shame we're having that boy over there.

quotes.speaker: Jerome Bettis
quotes.summary_phrase: Jerome Bettis describes his iconic touchdown run against Chicago
quotes.excerpt: I ran the first guy over, then Urlacher came and I ran him over.
quotes.quote: It's a muddy game because it's snowing and the field is heated, so the snow turned into mud. He was sliding around and so coach pulls him and put me in. I go to work. There's this iconic play at the end of the game that we close them out and it's this big run that I had and it's a touchdown run. I ran the first guy over, then Urlacher came and I ran him over and then scored a touchdown right over top of him.

quotes.speaker: Jerome Bettis
quotes.summary_phrase: Jerome Bettis and Brian Urlacher traded shoes after the game
quotes.excerpt: I went to his locker room and gave him the shoes that I wore.

text_blocks.speaker: Jerome Bettis
text_blocks.text: After the game, we traded shoes. I went to his locker room and gave him the shoes that I wore and he took I took his shoes. So that wasn't the idea, but he has the cleats. So the people wanted him to sign this picture. I ain't signing that picture. So he would always be mad, man. All these people trying to get me to sign this picture. I ain't signing that picture.

quotes.speaker: Jerome Bettis
quotes.summary_phrase: Jerome Bettis on his friendship with Donovan McNabb
quotes.excerpt: Donovan McNabb. He was a really, really, has been a really, really, really good friend.
quotes.quote: Donovan McNabb. He was a really, really, has been a really, really, really good friend for a long time and I would have loved to see us try to go get a championship because he was he was special and he doesn't get the credit he deserves because they never could win it. But they were they were good for a lot of years and he was a dynamic quarterback.
